task: Wrap five JS command-execution paths in runner-bridge.js and renderer.js with cmdlog store instrumentation, streaming PTY TextDecoder decode, ANSI stripping, and node:test coverage.

key_reasoning.reason: Four components touched: runner-bridge.js (wrapping 5 paths: runStream, runCapture, runFreshEnv, spawnPty, runSelfUpdate), renderer.js (re-pointing runUpdateCli from direct invoke to bridge.updater.runSelfUpdate), a new ansi-strip utility following the app-updater-utils.mjs precedent, and a new test file. runner-bridge.js is the core shared bridge for all command execution in the app; wrapping it affects every caller (runSmoke, startSignIn, runAction, runUpdateCli). Red flag: touches core shared utilities, bumped from M(3) to L(4).

Two novel implementation paths with no codebase precedent: (1) streaming TextDecoder({ stream: true }) per spawnPty invocation — the existing base64/PTY path in terminal.js feeds raw bytes to xterm.js, not decoded text, so this pattern does not transfer; (2) ANSI escape sequence stripper that must correctly handle sequences split across engine:pty-data chunk boundaries after TextDecoder decode — a stateless regex applied per-chunk will corrupt split sequences, requiring a stateful approach or a regex tolerant of incomplete escapes at end-of-string. Nearest test precedent (pty-bridge.test.mjs) covers id-filtering and CR-005 cleanup but has no template for chunk-boundary ANSI stripping, triggering the edge-case auto-bump from M(3) to L(4). Streaming PTY TextDecoder decode is a real-time/streaming requirement, triggering the streaming red flag from L(4) to XL(5). Calibration note: M anchor EPMCDME-10202 scored Technical Risk S(2) for a purely pattern-following task; this task's streaming+chunk-boundary novelty justifies the higher score, while lower Affected Layers (S=2) keeps total within M band.

Technical Risk bumped L(4) → XL(5): streaming PTY TextDecoder decode is a real-time/streaming requirement.
